Sleep, resting heart rate, heart rate variability and recent training load each score from 0 to 100 against your own 28-day average. Weights are 0.35 sleep, 0.25 resting heart rate, 0.20 heart rate variability and 0.20 load, renormalised over the inputs that exist. Fewer than two inputs or fewer than seven days of baseline show no score. It is an estimate of how the day compares with your usual, never a health claim.
How the weight trend is calculated

Each weigh-in is entered on its local day. The line is an exponentially weighted trend with a seven-day half-life, so one unusual scale reading moves it little. The weekly change is the trend seven days apart, and the goal estimate divides the remaining weight by that rate. The raw readings stay in the table and in the timeline.

In is the energy in the food you logged. Out is your basal metabolic rate from Mifflin-St Jeor plus the energy of your steps plus logged and imported workouts. Step energy uses a 0.762 m stride at a 3 MET walking pace. The burn is shown as a range because none of it is measured directly: five percent around basal rate, 25 percent around step energy and 20 percent around a workout. Net is in minus out, so its range runs the other way.
How the macro bars are calculated

Each bar is the day\'s grams of that macronutrient divided by its target. Targets come from your saved nutrition target; a day without one shows the bars without a target. Fibre is shown beside the three energy macros because it is a target the app tracks, not a source of calories.

A day\'s steps come from one source, chosen by your priority list. Raw readings from every source stay in the database. Active minutes and distance are reported by the winning source when it provides them; the app does not estimate them from a step count.

Volume is the sum of weight times reps over the work sets in a session. Warm-up sets are counted as sets but not added to volume. The weekly bar is the total for the week starting Monday. Bodyweight sets add no external load.
How sets per muscle are calculated

Every work set credits the muscles its exercise lists. A set that names two muscles credits both, so the totals are a picture of where the work went, not a partition of the whole. The window is the last seven days.

Each cell is one day. A day darkens with the number of work sets logged against the busiest day in the window, in five steps. Empty days stay empty; the grid never fills a gap. The window is the last twelve weeks.
How body fat change is calculated

Each reading carries the method it came from: a scale\'s bioimpedance, a tape measurement with the US Navy equation, a DEXA scan, or a typed value. The chart plots readings on their local day and compares the latest with the first in the window. Different methods are not blended into one number; the sheet names the method of each end.

A night is the sleep your device or you recorded, attributed to the local day it started. Durations are summed from the night\'s intervals. The 14-night debt is the shortfall against your sleep need, counted only when a night is below it. Consistency is the standard deviation of nightly duration across the window.

Stages arrive from the source that recorded them. Awake, REM, light and deep are drawn in that order with their names beside the bar, so the chart survives colour blindness. A night without stage data shows only its total duration; the app does not invent a stage split.

Protein is the sum of the protein in the foods logged that day. The target comes from your saved nutrition target or the suggestion from your profile and goal. Days without a meal are gaps, not zeros.
